title: argus repo configuration
description: Configuration schema for .argus/config.yml files. All keys are optional; a missing file is equivalent to a zero config. See internal/repoconfig/config.go.

base_branch.description: Base branch supervise/rebase/ship resolve worktrees and PRs against. Without this, argus falls back to its own default-branch detection.

worker_placement.description: Where a spawned worker's pane lands. Empty/unset behaves the same as "workspace".

launcher.description: Command started in each worker pane after cd into its worktree. Empty/unset falls back to argus's own default (claude --permission-mode auto). An explicit --launcher flag on supervise still overrides this.

forge.description: Self-hosted forge API shape for a host outside argus's auto-detected allowlist (github.com, gitlab.com, codeberg.org). An explicit --forge flag on ship/supervise/worktree prune still overrides this. Empty/unset behaves like auto-detect, which still refuses any other unrecognized host.

worktree_dir.description: Where a spawned worker's worktree is created. Empty/unset defaults to <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<branch>. A relative value is joined under the repo root, so ".." points at a sibling-of-repo convention (<parent>/<branch>); an absolute value is used as-is. Changing this shifts the worktree's nesting depth relative to the original checkout — see worktree_bootstrap_command's own note if that command hardcodes a relative hop count back to it.

brief_note.description: Free-text note appended verbatim to every generated worker brief.
examples: Add a focused test and keep make ci green.

review_note.description: Free-text note appended verbatim to the reviewer's prompt.
examples: Pay extra attention to internal/supervisor changes.

ship_verify_command.description: Controller-side gate command run before ship commits, in addition to argus's own built-in hook detection. Empty/unset runs no extra command.

gate_verify_command.description: Shell command the gate runs in a worker's worktree once it reaches a terminal phase, before a verdict is recorded. This is also the general-purpose escape hatch for any repo-specific mechanical rule ReviewPolicy has no dedicated field for (max_diff_lines/proof_required_paths/always_review_paths are a closed set): express the rule as a script that exits non-zero on violation and its failure becomes an unwaivable escalation, no argus code change needed. It only fires at that one gate checkpoint, not continuously during planning/working, so a violation surfaces at review time rather than the moment it's introduced. Empty/unset skips this check. (Renamed from verify_command — the old name still works, see Config.Deprecated.)

worktree_bootstrap_command.description: Shell command run once, synchronously, in a freshly created worktree, right after `git worktree add` succeeds and before the worker's agent is spawned. A non-zero exit fails worktree creation. Use this to bootstrap gitignored per-developer local config (env files, local settings) that only exists in the original checkout. Empty/unset runs no extra command. It runs with cwd already at the resolved worktree_dir location, after `git worktree add` already succeeded there — it must never attempt to create or relocate the worktree itself (git will refuse, surfacing as a raw git error wrapped in this command's own failure message). A script that hardcodes a relative hop count back to the original checkout (e.g. `cp ../../.env .env`, assuming the default two-levels-deep layout) breaks if worktree_dir changes the nesting depth; prefer deriving the repo root at runtime (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) over a hardcoded hop count. (Renamed from worktree_setup_command, itself renamed from worktree_setup_cmd — both old names still work, see Config.Deprecated.)

ship_lint.description: Deprecated: renamed to ship_verify_command. Still accepted — argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read — but new configs should use the new name.

verify_command.description: Deprecated: renamed to gate_verify_command. Still accepted — argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read — but new configs should use the new name.

worktree_setup_cmd.description: Deprecated: renamed to worktree_bootstrap_command. Still accepted — argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read — but new configs should use the new name.

worktree_setup_command.description: Deprecated: renamed to worktree_bootstrap_command. Still accepted — argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read — but new configs should use the new name.

title_prefix_template.description: Required PR/commit title prefix, mechanically enforced by ship on whatever title it ends up using (worker-reported, forge-fetched, branch-derived, or --title), regardless of the worker's self-reported title. "{issue}" is replaced with --jira-issue's key if set, else "#<--issue>" if set, else empty. A title that already starts with the rendered prefix is left alone; otherwise the prefix is prepended. Empty/unset applies no enforcement.

review_effort.description: Reasoning effort for --review. Without this, the review command's own default wins.

owner_stale_after.description: How long a worktree's owner-lease heartbeat (see internal/ownership, .claude/argus/owner.json) may go quiet before a mismatched caller on rework/rebase/ship/worker answer proceeds (with a logged notice) instead of being refused. A Go duration string. Empty/unset falls back to the built-in default (30m). An explicit --owner-stale-after flag still overrides this.

max_diff_lines.description: Review gate: diffs larger than this (insertions+deletions) escalate. 0 disables the ceiling; unset/null falls back to the gate's own default.

rework_budget.description: Restart budget: total rework rounds a worktree may ever be dispatched for, across every separate `argus rework` invocation over its lifetime — distinct from --max-rounds, which only bounds one invocation's own loop. Exceeding it records an unwaivable rework-budget-exceeded verdict instead of dispatching another round. 0 disables the budget; unset/null falls back to rework's own default.

allow.description: Extra tool-permission patterns granted to workers, on top of argus's toolchain-neutral defaults.

proof_required_paths.description: Path globs whose changes require real_world_proof in a worker's report before the review gate accepts it. Setting this key entirely replaces argus's own built-in default list rather than merging with it.

always_review_paths.description: Path globs that always escalate to human/reviewer attention regardless of diff size. Setting this key entirely replaces argus's own built-in default list rather than merging with it. The one exception is .argus/config.yml itself: it is always checked regardless of this list, since it governs next run's own gate policy and can't be allowed to silently drop out by omission.
